name: Oath of the Hearth
status: HOMEBREW - not official Wizards of the Coast content. All official rules in this canon take precedence over this subclass except where the subclass explicitly overrides them.
patron: Aesis the Shepherd, an Astera governing fields of grain and the hearth within the home.
tenets: Tend the hearth with holy effort.
Gather to the hearth those in need of warmth and rest.
Guard the hearth with the flame within and the flame without.

structuralAudit.verdict: Structurally sound. The subclass follows the official 2024 Paladin subclass template exactly: oath spells at levels 3/5/9/13/17 (two per tier), a Channel Divinity option at level 3, an aura upgrade at level 7, a feature at level 15, and a capstone at level 20.
structuralAudit.spellTierCheck: PASS. Every oath spell is of a level for which a Paladin has slots at the level it is granted: L3 grants level 1 spells (slots at Paladin 1), L5 grants level 2 (slots at 5), L9 grants level 3 (slots at 9), L13 grants level 4 (slots at 13), L17 grants level 5 (slots at 17).
structuralAudit.powerLevelVsOfficial: Aura of Solace at level 7 grants Resistance to three damage types, which is exactly the benchmark set by Oath of the Ancients' Aura of Warding (Necrotic, Psychic, Radiant). Fire, Cold and Psychic are collectively somewhat more commonly encountered than Necrotic, Psychic and Radiant, so it is at or slightly above the official power curve - within tolerance, not broken.

oathSpellRules: These are always prepared and do NOT count against the Prepared Spells number, but they otherwise count as Paladin spells for you. You still must expend a spell slot of the appropriate level to cast them (except where a feature grants a free casting).

features.name: Hearthfire Manifest
features.rawText: You bear the manifestation of the Hearthfire both within and without. This manifestation appears in a form you choose, such as a small floating ember, a dancing flame, or a spirit. The manifestation sheds Bright Light for 10 feet and Dim Light for 10 additional feet. If this manifestation goes beyond 30 feet from you, it is extinguished. It can be summoned or dismissed as a Bonus Action. As a Reaction, you can expend one use of your Channel Divinity and issue a command word, causing the Essence of the Hearth to transform into a flaming cloak. The cloak immediately grants you Temporary Hit Points equal to your Paladin level plus your spellcasting ability modifier. When you are hit by a melee attack, the creature takes 1d10 Fire damage in retaliation. This effect lasts until the Temporary Hit Points are depleted.

mechanics.light: Bright Light 10 ft, Dim Light 10 ft beyond
mechanics.leash: Extinguished if it goes more than 30 feet from you
mechanics.retaliation: 1d10 Fire to a creature that hits you with a melee attack
mechanics.duration: Until the Temporary Hit Points are depleted

features.name: Aura of Solace
features.rawText: You and your allies have Resistance to Fire, Cold, and Psychic damage while in your Aura of Protection.

mechanics.shape: Follows Aura of Protection: 10-foot Emanation from you, 30 feet at Paladin level 18
mechanics.effect: Resistance to Fire, Cold, and Psychic damage
mechanics.inactiveWhen: Aura of Protection is inactive while you have the Incapacitated condition, so Aura of Solace is too.
mechanics.emanationNote: Aura of Solace inherits Aura of Protection's Emanation. You are inside it because Aura of Protection's wording ('You and your allies in the aura') overrides the general rule that an Emanation excludes its origin.

features.name: Smoldering Smite
features.rawText: The flame of the hearth is fierce enough to burn into your smites. Whenever you use a Magic action to cast Divine Smite, add 1d8 Fire damage to each smite. This Fire damage ignores resistance and immunity to Fire damage.

mechanics.pierces: Resistance AND Immunity to Fire damage

features.name: Hearth Warden
features.rawText: As a Bonus Action, you imbue your Aura of Protection with the blazing flames of the hearth for 10 minutes, or until you end it. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest. You can also restore your use of it by expending a level 5 spell slot (no action required). Edge of Flame: Once per turn, you may choose one creature within your Aura, including yourself, to regain 10 HP. Punishing Flame: Any creature you choose within your aura may add Fire damage to their weapon attacks in an amount equal to your Charisma modifier. Swift Flame: Whenever you cast a spell that has a casting time of an action, you can cast it using a Bonus Action instead.

mechanics.duration: 10 minutes or until you end it
mechanics.recharge: Long Rest, or expend a level 5 spell slot (no action required)
mechanics.edgeOfFlame: Once per turn, one creature in the aura (including you) regains 10 HP
mechanics.punishingFlame: Chosen creatures in the aura add Fire damage equal to your Charisma modifier to weapon attacks
mechanics.swiftFlame: Spells with a casting time of an Action can be cast as a Bonus Action instead

errata.problem: The text says 'Whenever you use a Magic action to cast Divine Smite'. In 2024, Divine Smite's casting time is 'Bonus Action, taken immediately after hitting a target with a Melee weapon or an Unarmed Strike'. It is NEVER a Magic action. As written, the trigger condition can never be satisfied and the feature does nothing.
errata.cause: Almost certainly written against 2014 rules, where Divine Smite was a class feature rather than a spell, or a misunderstanding of the 2024 Magic action.
errata.recommendedFix: Replace with: 'Whenever you cast a spell whose name includes Smite, add 1d8 Fire damage to that spell's damage. This Fire damage ignores Resistance and Immunity to Fire damage.'
errata.narrowerAlternative: 'Whenever you cast Divine Smite, add 1d8 Fire damage.' This is the minimal fix that preserves the literal intent but excludes Searing Smite, which is thematically odd for a fire subclass.
errata.appAction: Do not silently implement either version. Present the conflict to the player, offer both fixes as a configurable setting, and default to the broader 'any Smite spell' version with a visible flag that it is a house ruling.

errata.problem: 'add 1d8 Fire damage to each smite' - 'each smite' is undefined. If the trigger is a single casting of Divine Smite, there is only one smite, so 'each' is meaningless. It may be intended to mean every Smite spell, or every attack in the turn.
errata.recommendedFix: Adopt the HEARTH-01 broad fix, which resolves the ambiguity: 1d8 Fire is added once, to the damage of the Smite spell being cast.
errata.appAction: Flag as a DM ruling. Do not apply the 1d8 to each of multiple attacks - that reading is far above the official power curve.

errata.problem: The cloak is activated 'As a Reaction' but no trigger is defined. 2024 requires every Reaction to state its trigger: 'A Reaction is a special action taken in response to a trigger defined in the Reaction's description.' Without a trigger the feature cannot be legally used.
errata.note: No official Paladin Channel Divinity option uses a Reaction; they use a Bonus Action or the Magic action. This is a genuine departure.
errata.recommendedFix: Define the trigger explicitly. Suggested: 'As a Reaction, which you take when you or a creature you can see within 30 feet takes damage, you can expend one use of your Channel Divinity...' Alternatively convert to a Bonus Action to match official Channel Divinity options.
errata.appAction: Require the player to record a chosen trigger with DM approval, then enforce it. Default suggestion: 'when you take damage'.

errata.problem: The cloak lasts 'until the Temporary Hit Points are depleted'. In 2024 Temporary Hit Points DO NOT STACK - when you gain new Temporary Hit Points you choose to keep the old pool or take the new one. Taking any other source of Temporary Hit Points (Heroism, Inspiring Leader, Orc Adrenaline Rush, a Chef treat, Aid does not apply) REPLACES the cloak's pool, which by the feature's own wording ends the cloak.
errata.recommendedFix: Add: 'The cloak lasts for 1 minute, or until the Temporary Hit Points granted by this feature are reduced to 0, whichever comes first. Gaining Temporary Hit Points from another source does not end this effect.' This decouples the duration from the temp HP pool.
errata.appAction: MANDATORY WARNING. If the cloak is active and the player gains Temporary Hit Points from another source, the app must prompt: 'Accepting these Temporary Hit Points will replace your Hearthfire cloak pool and end the cloak. Continue?'

errata.problem: The retaliation clause has no limit on frequency. 'When you are hit by a melee attack, the creature takes 1d10 Fire damage' triggers on every melee hit, with no once-per-turn or once-per-round cap and no Reaction cost.
errata.comparison: The Fire Shield spell (level 4) deals 2d8 on the same trigger with the same lack of cap, so unlimited retaliation is not unprecedented. However, Fire Shield is a level 4 spell with a hard 10-minute duration; the cloak is a level 3 Channel Divinity whose duration is tied to a temp HP pool that can be large.
errata.assessment: Acceptable as written at low levels. At level 20 with a large temp HP pool this could run for a very long time.
errata.recommendedFix: Optional: cap the duration at 1 minute (see HEARTH-04), which naturally bounds it.
errata.appAction: Implement as written but display the total retaliation damage dealt per encounter so the DM can see the real numbers.

errata.problem: Unclear whether the manifestation must be summoned before the cloak can be used, and whether summoning it costs a separate Bonus Action from the Reaction that activates the cloak. Also undefined: how the manifestation moves, whether it occupies a space, whether it can be attacked or targeted, and whether it provides light while worn as a cloak.
errata.recommendedFix: Rule that the manifestation must be active to transform into the cloak; that it moves with you automatically (treat it as an effect on your person, not a creature or object); that it cannot be attacked or damaged; and that the cloak sheds the same light as the manifestation.
errata.appAction: Record these as a house-ruling block the player fills in once with DM approval.

errata.problem: The text says 'You and your allies have Resistance to Fire, Cold, and Psychic damage while in your Aura of Protection'. It does not state that the aura is inactive while you are Incapacitated, but Aura of Protection itself is. It should inherit that limitation.
errata.recommendedFix: Explicitly state: 'This benefit is inactive while you have the Incapacitated condition, as with your Aura of Protection.'
errata.appAction: Implement the inheritance. It follows from the wording 'while in your Aura of Protection' - if the aura is inactive, nobody is in it.

errata.problem: Warding Bond is granted as an oath spell at Paladin level 5, but it is ALSO on the standard 2024 Paladin spell list. Half of that tier's grant is therefore wasted - the player could already have prepared it.
errata.assessment: Not a rules break, just a design inefficiency. The other eight oath spells are all off-list and genuinely expand the class.
errata.recommendedFix: Optional flavour-preserving swap: replace Warding Bond with Flaming Sphere (level 2 Conjuration, a controllable rolling fire that deals damage each turn) or Heat Metal (level 2, punishes armoured foes). Both are more on-theme for fire and neither is on the Paladin list.
errata.appAction: At minimum, DEDUPLICATE. Never let Warding Bond be selected as one of the seven prepared spells while it is already granted by the oath. This is the most likely place your app silently wastes a resource.

errata.problem: 'This Fire damage ignores resistance and immunity to Fire damage.' Ignoring IMMUNITY is stronger than any official feat or feature in the 2024 rules. Elemental Adept and the Poisoner feat ignore Resistance only. Boon of Irresistible Offense (a level 19+ Epic Boon) ignores Resistance only.
errata.assessment: This is a deliberate homebrew upgrade beyond the official power curve. At level 15 it is not game-breaking - 1d8 is small - but it sets a precedent the DM should be aware of.
errata.recommendedFix: Leave as written if the DM likes it; it is thematically strong and numerically minor. If the DM wants official parity, change 'resistance and immunity' to 'Resistance'.
errata.appAction: Flag as above-curve in any DM-facing view. No player-facing change needed.

errata.problem: 'Any creature you choose within your aura may add Fire damage to their weapon attacks in an amount equal to your Charisma modifier.' Ambiguous scope: is this one creature, or all of them? Also undefined: once per turn per creature, or on every attack?
errata.recommendedFix: Suggested: 'Each creature you choose within your aura adds Fire damage equal to your Charisma modifier to each weapon attack that hits.' At a 30-foot aura (level 18+) with a full party this is strong but appropriate for a level 20 capstone.
errata.appAction: Present the ambiguity; default to 'all chosen creatures, on every hit' with a DM-approval flag.

errata.problem: 'Whenever you cast a spell that has a casting time of an action, you can cast it using a Bonus Action instead.' This is very powerful - it lets you cast Flame Strike or Destructive Wave as a Bonus Action and still take the Attack action.
errata.mitigatingFactor: The 2024 one-spell-slot-per-turn rule caps the abuse: you still cannot cast two slotted spells in one turn. Swift Flame converts an Action into a Bonus Action, it does not let you double up on slots.
errata.assessment: Strong but defensible for a level 20 capstone that costs a Bonus Action to activate, lasts 10 minutes, and runs once per Long Rest.
errata.appAction: Implement, but enforce the one-slot-per-turn rule strictly on top of it. Also note the internal tension: Swift Flame wants your Bonus Action for spells, while Divine Smite also wants your Bonus Action. You still get only one Bonus Action per turn.

errata.problem: 'Once per turn, you may choose one creature within your Aura, including yourself, to regain 10 HP.' Does not state what action, if any, this costs.
errata.recommendedFix: Rule it as requiring no action, once per turn, as part of the aura's ongoing effect. This matches the phrasing and is appropriate for a capstone.
errata.appAction: Default to 'no action required, once per turn'.

combos.name: The Bonfire (level 13+)
combos.effect: The cloak deals 1d10 Fire and Fire Shield deals 2d8 to any creature that hits you with a melee attack. Together that is roughly 14 damage automatically, per melee hit, with no save, no attack roll, and no action cost.
combos.why: Fire Shield has no Concentration requirement, so it stacks with whatever you are concentrating on. Against a swarm of attackers you become an automatic area-damage effect. Choose the CHILL shield for Cold damage if the enemy is Fire-immune.

combos.name: The Wall and the Hearth (level 13+)
combos.effect: Cast Wall of Fire as a 20-foot-diameter ring with the damaging side facing OUTWARD, and stand your party inside it. Enemies take 5d8 to enter and 5d8 for every turn they end near it. Your allies inside get your Charisma bonus to saves and Resistance to Fire, Cold and Psychic.
combos.why: This is the mechanical expression of the entire oath - you build a hearth on the battlefield and everyone inside it is safe. Most character tools only surface the straight-wall version of Wall of Fire; make sure yours shows the ring.

combos.name: Damage Relocation (level 7+)
combos.effect: Warding Bond gives an ally Resistance to all damage and transfers what they take to you. If your DM rules that transferred damage keeps its type, your Aura of Solace halves it AGAIN for Fire, Cold and Psychic. A 20-point fire hit becomes 10 to them and 5 to you.
combos.why: You are not reducing damage, you are moving it onto the character best built to absorb it, and then halving it a second time. Ask your DM to confirm the damage-type ruling - it is the load-bearing assumption.

combos.name: The Free-Cast Opener (level 5+)
combos.effect: The 2024 one-slot-per-turn rule restricts EXPENDING slots. Your free Divine Smite expends none. RAW you can cast a slotted spell with your Action and free-cast Divine Smite with your Bonus Action on the same turn, once per Long Rest.
combos.why: This is your single biggest burst turn. Save it. Confirm with your DM before relying on it.

combos.name: Topple into Smite (level 5+)
combos.effect: Attack 1 with a Topple weapon (Battleaxe, Maul, Quarterstaff, Lance, Trident). On a hit, force a Constitution save or the target is Prone. Attack 2 then has Advantage against a Prone target within 5 feet. Advantage roughly doubles your crit chance, and a crit doubles all your Smite dice.
combos.why: The highest-damage reliable line a level 7 Paladin has, and it also gives your whole party Advantage on their melee attacks against that target.

combos.name: Faerie Fire Opening (level 3+)
combos.effect: Round one, from up to 60 feet, blanket the enemy cluster in a 20-foot Cube. Everything that fails a Dexterity save gives your entire party Advantage on attacks against it for a minute, and cannot benefit from the Invisible condition.
combos.why: Faerie Fire uses your Action but not your Bonus Action, so you can still summon your Hearthfire Manifest the same turn. It targets Dexterity, which is the save that heavy brutes fail - the opposite profile from your Smites.
